subject: Architecture
title: Hindu Temple Mountains: Homes for the Gods
description: A short lesson to help you apply Hindu Temple Mountains: Homes for the Gods.

hook.text: Hindu temples aren't just buildings — they represent Mount Meru, the cosmic mountain at the center of the universe.

buildup.text: The shikhara tower rises over the sanctum, symbolizing the peak. The temple is a map of the cosmos in stone.

discovery.text: Every room, corridor, and decoration is placed according to sacred geometry called Vastu Shastra.

twist.text: Some temples are carved from a single rock — the Kailasa Temple was excavated downward, removing 200,000 tons.

climax.text: Angkor Wat in Cambodia is the largest Hindu temple ever built — a city-sized mountain for Vishnu.

punchline.text: Every Hindu temple is a mountain, a universe, and a doorway at once.

quiz.question: What does a Hindu temple's tower symbolize?
options: The tree of life reaching toward the sun
The hand of the creator pointing upward

details.summary: Hindu temples represent Mount Meru — the cosmic mountain at the center of the universe in Hindu cosmology. Their towering shikhara (spire) forms the mountain peak, while concentric enclosures represent descending cosmic realms.
details.whyItMatters: Hindu temples transform cosmology into architecture. Every element — from the mountain-shaped tower to the dark inner sanctum — represents a specific aspect of the universe.
takeaways: Temples represent Mount Meru, the cosmic mountain center
The shikhara spire forms the peak; concentric enclosures descend
The dark innermost chamber symbolizes cosmic stillness

faq.question: Why is the inner sanctum of a Hindu temple so dark?
faq.answer: The garbhagriha (womb chamber) is deliberately windowless — a cave within the mountain. Darkness represents the unmanifest state of the divine before creation.

faq.question: What is the difference between North and South Indian temple styles?
faq.answer: North Indian (Nagara) temples feature a curved beehive-shaped tower that tapers to a point. South Indian (Dravidian) temples have pyramidal towers built in stepped horizontal layers called gopurams. Both represent the cosmic mountain but use very different formal vocabularies.
